paper_title: Upper Limit on the QCD Axion Mass from Isolated Neutron Star Cooling
notes: Buschmann, Dessert, Foster, Long, Safdi (2021): axion cooling of five isolated neutron stars (four Magnificent Seven NSs + PSR J0659). Headline model-dependent result is m_a < 16 meV (95% CL) for the KSVZ QCD axion. Reported here is the model-independent phenomenological bound quoted in the main text (and shown in Fig. S5): for an axion coupled only to neutrons, |g_ann| < 1.3e-9 at 95% confidence (proton-only case: |g_app| < 1.5e-9, with g_an set to zero, not reported). The paper defines L = (C_N/2f_a) psibar_N gamma^mu gamma_5 psi_N d_mu a with g_aNN = C_N m_N/f_a, identical to the canonical g_an normalisation, so no conversion applied. The bound comes from thermal axion emission (bremsstrahlung + Cooper-pair breaking/formation) and is independent of m_a for masses well below the NS core temperature (~10^8 K ~ 10 keV); it is therefore given as a flat line from 1e-12 eV up to ~10 keV (the mass range is not explicitly stated in the paper). Limit profiles over EOS (BSk22/24/25), superfluidity models, NS masses and envelope composition; not a dark-matter search, so no local DM density assumed.
